title: The Electric Car Revolution
description: How electric vehicles are distributed around the world — and how fast the fleet has grown.

items.label: The Market Leaders
items.note: China, Europe, and the United States together account for roughly 95% of all global EV sales. The rest of the world is largely yet to adopt.

items.label: Sales vs. Total Fleet
items.note: While 1 in 4 new cars sold globally is now electric, they still make up only about 5% of the total vehicle stock on the world's roads — existing combustion engines take decades to retire.

items.label: The Per-Capita Champion
items.note: Norway leads the world in EV density. Massive tax exemptions and toll discounts mean roughly 1 in 3 cars currently driving on Norwegian roads is electric.

sections.heading: Electric Vehicles per 1,000 People — by Country
sections.caption: Countries vary enormously in EV density. Small, wealthy Nordic nations lead; large emerging economies have very low per-capita figures despite high absolute numbers.

sections.heading: Global Electric Car Stock — Growth 2015 to 2025
sections.caption: The world electric car fleet has grown from under 1 million in 2015 to around 70 million by 2025 — doubling roughly every two years through the early 2020s.
